summary: Trailing CRLF conversion by intermediary suppresses final metadata event after SSE resume
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a short network interruption and SSE resume, the final metadata event ("id":"session_end", "status":"complete") is missing from the resumed stream. Impact: downstream client never receives final metadata which triggers end-of-response processing; customers observe truncated final sentence and no end-of-stream payload. Environment: prod us-east, Dedicated instance for LuminaDocs, model pinned to redwood-2-medium.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a long streaming completion via SSE against the hosted endpoint using the customer's proxy stack (CloudEdge + header-rewrite layer).
2) Simulate a short TCP-level disconnect (~1-3s) between client and edge by TCP RST or by toggling client network.
3) Allow the client to reconnect using the same session token and resume as normal.
4) Observe resumed stream payloads and check for the terminal metadata event ("event: metadata\ndata: {..session_end..}\n\n").

Observed behavior: In a reproducible subset (~12% of attempts), the resumed stream contains the final text but the separate metadata SSE event is missing. The last chunk of text is present but the terminal metadata event that client relies on to finalize the response is suppressed.

Expected behavior: Final metadata event should appear after resumed content in every successful resume sequence.

Relevant logs/attachments: Uploaded client capture (sse-chunk-trace-0311.log), edge proxy logs showing a rewrite step (edge-rewrite-0311.log), request_id: req-9b3f2c2a. Attached sample client trace shows CRLF sequences inserted by intermediary that appear to coalesce the terminal metadata event into the previous data frame and the event separator (blank line) is dropped.
comments: 2026-03-11 Priya Desai (customer): We see the final JSON metadata event for session_end missing about 1 in 8 resumes. The text completes but our client waits for the metadata and times out. Attaching traces.

2026-03-11 Diego Alvarez (support triage): Acknowledged. Marking P1 due to production impact. Requested full edge proxy logs and the client's raw SSE stream. Assigned to Diego for initial repro and correlation with edge logs.

2026-03-12 Diego Alvarez (support): Initial triage: reproduced locally when an intermediary converts lone LF to CRLF on boundary and collapses the blank-line event separator. Suspect intermediary is normalizing line endings during header-rewrite stage. Raised to infra for proxy inspection. Related to odd behavior seen in SUP-842117 but distinct due to explicit CRLF insertion.

2026-03-12 SRE (Elena Novak): Observed edge-rewrite rules that run a small transform for inline header updates. Confirmed a path where LF -> CRLF conversion happens because the proxy invokes a text-normalize filter for HTTP/1.1 to maintain legacy backends. Disabled normalization in a canary; possible fix in that config change reduced occurrence in canary by ~90%.
2026-03-13 LuminaDocs (customer): Canary disables helped; we still see 1/50 failures. Customer requests durable fix and rollback prevention steps. Asked for timeline and patch plan.

2026-03-14 Diego Alvarez (support): Eng investigating runtime behavior where resumed frames are reassembled and rely on blank-line separators. Edge config change being tested and unit tests added. Will provide patch PR link when available.
investigation:
Investigative summary: Reproducer built using customer proxy stack and SSE client. When an intermediary changes line endings from LF to CRLF across the event separator (i.e., transforms "

" into "
" + "
" but collapses one of the separators), the SSE parser on the client sees the metadata event merged into prior data or loses the final empty line used to delimit events. The server runtime emits correct events in origin logs; loss occurs in the rewrite layer. See edge proxy logs: request_id req-9b3f2c2a shows transformation at byte offset 14321.

Hypothesis 1: Text-normalize filter in edge-proxy rewrites streaming payload boundaries, inadvertently removing the blank-line separator between SSE events when the reconnection resume produces a boundary that matches heuristic. This causes the client's SSE parser to consider metadata as continuation of previous event or skip it.

Hypothesis 2: In resumption path, small resume fragments result in event-buffer reassembly where the edge's chunking + LF->CRLF normalization recombines frames differently than expected, exposing a race between rewriter and connection drain.

Data: Canary change that disabled normalization reduced failure rate from ~12% to ~1-2% in LuminaDocs traffic for 48h. Origin logs (serving-runtime) show consistent event emission with session_end metadata present for every returned response. No change observed in model output; problem isolated to proxy rewrite behavior.
Logs & dashboards: edge-proxy/error-rate, streaming/late-metadata occurrences, request traces: https://grafana.internal/streams?var-request=req-9b3f2c2a

Repro notes: Created a synthetic client that toggles network for 1-3s and reissues resume. Reproducer attached as repro_crlf_resume.sh. Edge config disabled text-normalize filter in canary cluster 'edge-canary-3'.
resolution: Workaround: Disable text-normalize/line-ending rewrite filter on edge for affected customers or route dedicated instances to a non-rewriting path. LuminaDocs was routed to non-rewriting canary which reduced failures dramatically.

Permanent fix: Engineering (edge team) to update proxy rewrite logic to preserve SSE event separators. Patch will: (1) treat streaming responses as binary-safe and skip LF/CRLF normalization for Content-Type: text/event-stream and chunked Transfer-Encoding; (2) add a unit test to ensure blank-line separators survive boundary rewriting; (3) add an integration test that simulates resume boundary cases.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/427 (edge: skip line-ending normalization for SSE streams) — currently in review by infra.

Rollout plan: Merge -> canary edge-canary-3 -> monitor for 72h -> gradual rollout to prod. Post-rollout monitoring: capture streaming/end-metadata-loss metric and reduce to 0 occurrences for 7d before closing ticket.

Follow-ups: Update runbook for streaming resume issues to include 'disable LF->CRLF normalization' as first mitigation. Consider adding a server-side 'resume-session' idempotent marker event that is tolerant to line-ending transforms.
Status: Fix in review; customer routed to canary and monitoring shows residual failure rate ~0.5% in 24h. Will keep ticket open until 7d stable post-prod rollout.
